newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's economy grows by 4.1 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Romania's economy grows by 4.1 pct in 1996.

text.p: Romania's gross domestic product (GDP) rose 4.1 percent last year, down from a revised 7.1 percent in 1995, National Statistics Board's (CNS) preliminary data showed on Friday.
The 1995 growth was revised up to 7.1 percent from a previous 6.9 percent, CNS said.
"Romania's economy expanded by 4.1 percent last year, with the GDP estimated at 109.5 trillion lei ($17.2 billion)," CNS president Pavel Wagner told a news conference.
Forecasts last year by Romania's former leftist government, ousted in November's general elections, put the 1996 GDP growth at 4.8 percent.
"Rises in industry and the construction sector were the main support of last year's economic growth," Wagner said.
Industry saw 9.9 percent growth last year, slightly up from 9.4 percent in 1995, while the construction sector rose by 7.0 percent on the previous year.
Farm output was 1.8 percent up last year against a 4.1 percent rise in 1995, while the services sector, which accounts for 35.6 percent of the GDP, grew by 2.4 percent in 1996.
The private sector's GDP stake grew to 52 percent in 1996 from 45 percent the previous year.
Year-on-year inflation surged to 56.9 percent last year from 27.8 percent in 1995, almost triple the 20-percent target agreed to under a loan accord with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The new coalition government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is now holding talks with IMF and World Bank experts on a package of reforms to resume credits that were suspended last year.
Last week, Ciorbea said Romania, forced to submit to an austerity programme to revamp its economy, would see negative growth in 1997.
But central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said there was scope to resume economic growth in the second half of this year. ($=6,069 lei)
